listenings.text: Okay, honest answer. The thing I avoid most is speaking English on the phone. In person I am fine, because I can see the person's face and I can point at things, but on the phone I panic. So last month I decided to do something about it, and it is very small: one phone call a week in English, even if it is thirty seconds, even if it is asking about opening hours. I have done four. They were all terrible and I do not care. What I want to improve this year is speaking without translating in my head first, because that is where the delay comes from. Everything else I can practise.

Good morning. Applications for the mentoring programme open today, and I want to explain the form, because students always get it wrong. There are three questions. What you enjoy doing. What you want to learn. And what you do not mind doing. The programme runs for four months, with one meeting every two weeks, so it is not heavy. Now, about that third question. Most students write something empty there, and it is a mistake, because that is the one the mentors read most carefully. It tells them how you actually work. Be specific and be honest. Deadline is the fifteenth.
